meta.name: 2026 Fantasy Football Research — Pick by Pick Approaches
meta.coverage: Detailed approaches supplied for draft slots 1.01 through 1.10. The document says 1.11 and 1.12 are forthcoming.
meta.role: Community strategy overlay. It does not replace Ballers ranks, community consensus, live ADP, injury adjustments, or tier data.

1.sourceAngle: The research compares Gibbs and Bijan Robinson: Bijan for player quality and the Stefanski rushing history; Gibbs for offensive line, offense, projected usage, and handcuff advantage.
1.edge: Lock the elite RB, stay disciplined at the 2/3 turn, and use the middle rounds for new-situation wide receivers instead of forcing quarterback.
1.checkpoint: In a 12-team room, expect QB and TE runs earlier than in 10-team drafts. The research prefers waiting on WR until roughly Rounds 4–7, where Egbuka, DeVonta Smith, and Carnell Tate may fit.
principles: After the first 8–11 running backs are gone, prioritize backs entering new systems.
Do not automatically double up at wide receiver at the 2/3 turn.
If an elite tight end is secured early, you can avoid the later TE run.
Treat the long waits between turns as real scarcity pressure, especially at QB and TE.

rounds.label: Round 1
rounds.objective: Make the 1.01 decision cleanly.
bullets: Current app call: Gibbs remains the clear 1.01.
Research case for Bijan: player quality plus Stefanski's Chubb-era rushing history.
Research case for Gibbs: better offense and line, more usage, and stronger handcuff structure.

rounds.label: Rounds 2–3
rounds.objective: Add an elite faller, an advantage TE, or the right second anchor.
bullets: Take Saquon Barkley, Justin Jefferson, or Drake London immediately if a 10-team-type fall reaches this turn.
Trey McBride and Brock Bowers are comfortable selections here.
If both elite tight ends are gone, do not force quarterback at the 4/5 turn.
Avoid leaving this turn with a fragile WR/WR construction just because the RB board feels uncomfortable.
warnings: Josh Jacobs and A.J. Brown share Bijan Robinson's bye.

rounds.label: Rounds 4–5
rounds.objective: Hit the new-situation WR/RB window.
bullets: Jaylen Waddle is a priority target in this build.
Quinshon Judkins is the featured new-system RB target.
Take Lamar Jackson or A.J. Brown immediately if either falls beyond expectation.
If you draft DeVonta Smith, do not later chase Makai Lemon without considering the overlap.
warnings: Many preferred middle-round WRs carry Week 10 byes.

rounds.label: Rounds 6–7
rounds.objective: Anticipate the QB/TE run before it controls you.
bullets: If Joe Burrow falls, this is the point to secure quarterback.
Harold Fannin Jr. is the first TE target in this window.
Carnell Tate is a receiver target; Zay Flowers is an immediate value if he falls.
Dak Prescott and Trevor Lawrence may not survive the next long wait.
warnings: If you already drafted Judkins, consider whether adding Fannin creates too much team concentration.

rounds.label: Rounds 8–9
rounds.objective: Protect the RB room and do not assume a QB returns.
bullets: Brian Robinson Jr. is the emphasized handcuff target.
Dak Prescott and Trevor Lawrence are unlikely to still be available if the room has started its run.

rounds.label: Rounds 10–11
rounds.objective: Finish unresolved premium positions and add upside RB depth.
bullets: Dak Prescott is still the quarterback target if he survives.
Jadarian Price is the late RB target.

rounds.label: Rounds 12–15
rounds.objective: Add volume bets and a second tight end when needed.
bullets: Wan'Dale Robinson is the named late receiver target.
Identify who will absorb Indianapolis targets rather than drafting only by name value.
A TE2 is reasonable if your starter carries role or health uncertainty.

decisions.when: Both McBride and Bowers are gone at the 2/3 turn
decisions.action: Do not react by forcing QB at 4/5. Keep the build focused on RB and the middle-round WR window.
Take the value and stop gambling on Dak or Lawrence making the full turn.

decisions.when: You secure an elite TE at 2/3
decisions.action: Use Rounds 6–9 on RB/WR depth and quarterback timing instead of joining the TE run.

alerts.title: Bye collisions
alerts.text: Jacobs and A.J. Brown share Bijan's bye; Judkins does as well. Week 10 also concentrates several preferred WRs.

alerts.title: QB and TE pressure
alerts.text: At the early turn, Dak and Trevor can disappear across the long gap. Decide before the run, not after it.

alerts.title: Team concentration
alerts.text: The research specifically warns against mindlessly pairing Judkins with Fannin or DeVonta Smith with a later Makai Lemon selection.

2.ideal: Whichever of Gibbs or Bijan remains
2.sourceAngle: This slot introduces a conditional three-RB opening when the elite tight ends are gone and multiple top-12 backs remain available.
2.edge: The 1.02 can turn positional scarcity into an advantage by opening RB-heavy, then attacking WR in Rounds 4–5 and premium positions in Rounds 6–7.
2.checkpoint: The three-RB path is conditional—not automatic. It is strongest when both elite tight ends are gone by 3.02 and three top-12 backs are still on the board.
principles: Use the three-RB approach only when the board creates it.
If top-12 RBs dry up, do not compound the problem by blindly doubling WR.
Plan team and bye-week stacks before making consecutive turn selections.
Rounds 6–7 can support QB, TE, or both after an RB-heavy opening.

rounds.label: Round 1
rounds.objective: Take the elite RB left at 1.02.
bullets: Choose between Gibbs and Bijan based on who remains.
The slot is designed for a Hero RB or Anchor RB opening.

rounds.label: Rounds 2–3
rounds.objective: Choose between elite TE, elite faller, or the three-RB path.
bullets: Immediate fall targets: Saquon Barkley, Justin Jefferson, Drake London, and Omarion Hampton.
Comfortable reaches include Trey McBride, Brock Bowers, and Chase Brown.
Trigger the three-RB approach only if both elite TEs are gone and three top-12 RBs remain.
If the top-12 RB tier is exhausted, avoid a reflexive WR/WR response.
warnings: Chase Brown shares Gibbs' bye; Jacobs and A.J. Brown share Bijan's bye.

rounds.label: Rounds 4–5
rounds.objective: Build the WR room after an RB-heavy opening.
bullets: Ladd McConkey and Jaylen Waddle are named receiver targets.
Quinshon Judkins is the new-system RB target when the board still supports another back.
Lamar Jackson or A.J. Brown become immediate values if they fall.
Track the Week 10 concentration among preferred WRs.
warnings: A Gibbs–Jameson Williams stack and a Burrow–Chase Brown stack require deliberate exposure decisions.

rounds.label: Rounds 6–7
rounds.objective: Use the flexibility created by the opening.
bullets: Joe Burrow is a take if he falls.
Prepare for simultaneous quarterback and tight-end runs.
Harold Fannin Jr., Carnell Tate, and a falling Zay Flowers are named targets.
Dak Prescott and Trevor Lawrence may not return.

rounds.label: Rounds 8–9
rounds.objective: Add handcuff value and avoid assuming premium availability.
bullets: Brian Robinson Jr. is the highlighted handcuff.
Dak and Trevor are probably gone if the run happened before this turn.

rounds.label: Rounds 10–11
rounds.objective: Resolve QB and add late RB upside.
bullets: Dak is still the QB target if he lasts.
Jadarian Price is the late RB target.

rounds.label: Rounds 12–15
rounds.objective: Finish with volume and contingency bets.
bullets: Wan'Dale Robinson is the late WR call.
Monitor the Indianapolis target tree.
Add a second tight end if the starter's role warrants it.

decisions.when: Both elite TEs are gone by 3.02 and three top-12 RBs are available
decisions.action: Use the three-RB approach, then draft WR in Rounds 4–5 and attack QB/TE in Rounds 6–7.

decisions.when: The top-12 RB tier is gone
decisions.action: Do not automatically double WR. Use tiers and positional scarcity to choose the best stabilizing pick.

decisions.when: You already have a correlated stack
decisions.action: Check bye weeks and team concentration before adding another player from the same offense.

alerts.title: Correlation check

alerts.title: Bye collisions
alerts.text: Chase Brown shares Gibbs' bye. Jacobs, A.J. Brown, and Judkins can collide with a Bijan start.

alerts.title: Premium window
alerts.text: An RB-heavy opening creates a strong Rounds 6–7 premium window, but Dak and Trevor may still vanish before the next turn.

3.sourceAngle: If Gibbs or Bijan falls, pivot to the 1.02 Hero/Anchor RB plan. Otherwise, an anchor-WR start requires at least one RB by the end of Round 3.
3.edge: Start with the elite target earner, secure an RB before the position cliffs, then attack the deep new-situation WR pocket.
3.checkpoint: The non-negotiable is one RB in the first three rounds. Rounds 8–9 are the preferred place to finish QB and TE if the earlier board does not deliver value.
principles: Do not double WR in Rounds 2–3 after opening with Chase.
Take at least one running back before leaving Round 3.
Use Rounds 4–5 for a new-situation receiver and, when available, Judkins.
Avoid eye candy in Rounds 6–7; premium positions are acceptable only when the RB/WR board is flat.

rounds.label: Round 1
rounds.objective: Anchor the WR room.
bullets: Ideal selection: Ja'Marr Chase.
If Bijan or Gibbs falls, pivot to the Hero/Anchor RB construction used at 1.02.

rounds.label: Rounds 2–3
rounds.objective: Secure at least one RB and avoid an unbalanced WR start.
bullets: Great RB targets: Omarion Hampton and Saquon Barkley; Jeremiyah Love is the next good target.
Round 3 can be best WR available or another RB.
If the top 11 RBs are gone: take an elite TE, then Nico Collins, then be willing to reach for RB in Round 3.
A Josh Allen start pushes Smith/Egbuka to WR2, Tyson to WR3, Downs to WR4, and makes Kittle or late TE targets more important.

rounds.label: Rounds 4–5
rounds.objective: Add a new-situation WR and protect against team-stack overexposure.
bullets: Targets: Zay Flowers, DeVonta Smith, Jaylen Waddle, and Emeka Egbuka.
Quinshon Judkins is the RB target.

rounds.label: Rounds 6–7
rounds.objective: Take conviction, not eye candy.
bullets: Carnell Tate is the WR target.
Jadarian Price and Rhamondre Stevenson are RB targets.
Jalen Hurts is a take if he falls.

rounds.label: Rounds 8–9
rounds.objective: Round out the starting lineup.
bullets: This is the preferred QB/TE double window.
QB targets: Trevor Lawrence and Dak Prescott.
TE targets: George Kittle and Dalton Kincaid.
If Kittle is selected, pair the risk with a late option such as Jake Tonges, Isaiah Likely, or Kenyon Sadiq.

rounds.label: Rounds 10–15
rounds.objective: Use positional runs, handcuffs, and role bets.
bullets: WRs: Wan'Dale Robinson, Deebo Samuel, and Tank Dell.
RBs: Jonathan Brooks and Rachaad White.
QBs: Tyler Shough and Kyler Murray.
TEs: Kenyon Sadiq, Isaiah Likely, and later Chig Okonkwo.

decisions.action: Take at least one RB by the end of Round 3. RB+TE, RB+RB, and RB+WR are valid; WR+WR is not the preferred path.
Take the elite TE if available, otherwise Nico Collins, then reach for the best RB in Round 3 rather than leaving the opening without one.
Accept a thinner WR/RB depth chart and deliberately target Smith/Egbuka, Tyson, Downs, Judkins, Stevenson, Corum, and the Kittle/late-TE windows.

alerts.text: Do not let attractive names create unnecessary RB/WR concentration from the same offense.

alerts.title: Round 8–9 finish
alerts.text: The slot's cleanest QB/TE completion point is Rounds 8–9; use the live availability windows to decide whether either position will survive.

4.ideal: Puka Nacua, unless Ja'Marr Chase falls
4.sourceAngle: A Gibbs/Bijan fall triggers the 1.02 RB plan. The standard build starts WR and prioritizes RB in Round 2 before the top-12 tier disappears.
4.edge: This slot can pair an elite WR with either an advantage TE or two early RBs, then exploit a strong new-situation WR/RB sequence in Rounds 4–5.
4.checkpoint: If the first three picks are two WRs plus a TE, the source wants two new-situation RB swings beginning in Rounds 4–5.
principles: After opening WR, Round 2 is the safer RB window.
Do not double WR in Rounds 2–3 without a clear plan for the RB cliff.
If you buy TE early, wait on QB and lean harder into RB.
The double-premium approach is viable only when later RB/WR targets are mapped in advance.

George Kittle is the TE target.

rounds.label: Rounds 10–15

RBs: Jonathan Brooks and Rachaad White.

TEs: Kenyon Sadiq, Isaiah Likely, then Chig Okonkwo.

Target Fannin around the end of Round 6 or wait for Likely/Sadiq around Rounds 10–11.
Use Rounds 4–5 for the best remaining new-situation RB and Rounds 6–7 for two upside receivers.

alerts.title: Round 2 RB pressure

alerts.title: QB return risk

alerts.title: Double-premium cost

5.ideal: Christian McCaffrey, unless Puka or Chase falls

5.edge: Stay flexible at 1.05: take the elite WR fall or CMC, then use Rounds 2–3 to establish the RB room before attacking new-situation WRs.
5.checkpoint: By the end of Round 5, the source wants an anchored WR room and at least one new-situation receiver, with premium positions mostly deferred unless value falls.
principles: Do not double WR in Rounds 2–3 after the CMC/RB start.
Achane and Omarion Hampton are Round 2 must-drafts in the source's structure.
Anchor WR in Round 3 unless an elite TE falls.

6.ideal: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, unless CMC, Puka, or Chase falls
6.sourceAngle: The source calls 1.06 the best spot for building a team full of great wide receivers, while still requiring one or two top-12 RBs and a new-situation RB.
6.edge: Middle-slot flexibility lets you react to tiers without a full turn wait. Use it to balance elite WR access with deliberate RB scarcity management.
6.checkpoint: Core goals: 1–2 top-12 RBs, one new-situation RB, and 1–2 upside WRs in new situations by the middle rounds. In 12-team, avoid doubling up on premium positions in Rounds 5–7 unless the value is undeniable.
principles: This is the source's preferred slot for a deep, high-quality WR room.
If two of the first three picks are WRs, prioritize—not necessarily force—RB in Round 4.

alerts.title: Best WR-build slot

7.theme: Anchor RB — or Anchor WR in select cases
7.ideal: Jonathan Taylor, unless JSN or CMC falls
7.sourceAngle: The source shifts to a balance framework: anchor rooms early, finish with upside, and aim for roughly three RBs plus three WRs after seven rounds.
7.edge: From 1.07, the first pick determines the Round 2 priority: RB start means WR priority unless RB value falls; WR start means RB priority.
7.checkpoint: After about seven rounds, the roster should feel balanced at roughly three RBs and three WRs, with at least one top-12 RB, one or two new-situation RBs, one or two upside new-situation WRs, and at least one rookie WR.
principles: Anchor your rooms, finish with upside.
If Round 1 is RB, prioritize WR unless top-12 RBs fall or Tier 3 WRs are gone.
If Round 1 is WR, secure RB in Round 2 to preserve access to the top 10–12 tier.
Once the roster is balanced, get ahead at QB or TE rather than adding redundant depth.
